title: When session_absent fires
body: The fact check found this line wrong. The plan said this event traces a session that lapsed mid-request. The code shows the guard redirects a lapsed session on admin pages and writes no record. The author rewrote it and dropped the row for a lapsed session.
was: A wrapped action logs `admin.action.session_absent` and stops at `createAdminAction`'s session check when no editor session reaches it, either because the session lapsed after the guard resolved it or because the guard never resolved one.
now: A wrapped action logs `admin.action.session_absent` and stops at its session check when no hook resolved an editor for the route: a route outside `/admin`, or a public admin path such as `/admin/login`. On a gated admin path the guard redirects a missing or expired session to `/admin/login` itself and writes no record.

title: The CSRF step in the check order
body: The fact check found a missing step. The first check also runs a CSRF check, which logs its own event. The author added it.
was: First, authentication runs through `createAdminAction`, which throws rather than answering `fail()`.
now: First, `createAdminAction` checks the session, then runs a double-submit CSRF check that logs `admin.action.csrf_refused` and throws `error(403)`. Both throw rather than answering `fail()`.

title: The reason a refusal records
body: The plan asked you to act on a refusal without saying how to tell refusals apart, so the author added this line after the fact check, from the code's own list of reasons.

title: Why production logs instead of throwing
body: The fact check and the author disagree on the reason this line gives.

sides.text: Its comment says an unaudited change “should not 500 a live site.”
“Worse than a gap in the audit trail” gives the reader the trade-off, and the comment implies it.

choices.label: Use the code's reason
choices.text: The handler returned on a path that never called `ctx.audit` and didn't return `fail()`, which is exempt because a rejected request changed nothing. Production logs instead of throwing because an unaudited change is a defect, but it shouldn't take a live site down with an error.

title: Keep the cairn CLI this early?
body: The `cairn logs` and `cairn health` lines sit here, before any event row, because a failed health check sends most readers to this page. The other choice is a short tooling section at the end, beside building your own queries.

choices.label: Move it to the end
choices.done: Move the CLI to the end
